caption: Candidate elimination on the worked example: S is filled in by the first positive and generalizes only once, at P2, then never moves, while each negative example trims G until only (?,Warm,?) survives. The last row is the final answer, and its S is the same hypothesis that Find-S returns.

spec.title: Candidate elimination, worked example
spec.aria: Five stacked steps of candidate elimination on the worked example: S starts as (∅,∅,∅) and G as (?,?,?); P1 makes S (Sunny,Warm,Strong), P2 generalizes S to (Sunny,Warm,?); N1 splits G into (Sunny,?,?) and (?,Warm,?); N2 leaves S at (Sunny,Warm,?) and G at (?,Warm,?).
